transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Could you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

Um... hi. I guess... well, I just keep getting stuck on this... this tiny uneven spot. Right around my nose and cheek. 

It's just... I see it a lot in photos, and under the bright lights at the store where I work. People say they don't see it, but... I don't know. It just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me. So... yeah. That's why I came in.
Do you feel that this uneven spot on your nose and cheek looks very different or abnormal compared to the rest of your face?

I mean... yeah, I guess so. It just... it stands out to me. Like I said, I see it every time I look at pictures, or when I'm under those harsh lights at the register. It just feels like... like it's right there. And even if my coworkers or whoever say it's nothing... I just feel like everyone sees it right away.
How long have you been feeling this way about the uneven spot? Has this been bothering you every day, or does it come and go?
Um... I don't know exactly when it started. A while, I guess. And... yeah, it's pretty much every day. It doesn't really go away.
Do these concerns about the uneven spot on your face cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Um... I guess a little bit. Mostly at work. My manager... well, they noticed I've been coming back from my breaks late. And I guess I've been moving slower at the register. I just... I'm trying to get promoted right now, and I'm worried it's making me look unreliable. So... yeah.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to cover it up—because of how much you think about that spot?

Um... yeah, I guess I do some of that. When I go on my breaks, I usually end up in the bathroom... just checking the mirror. I try to pull my hair around to cover it up better. And... I don't know, I just catch myself looking at the girls who come through my line and comparing my skin to theirs. That's... that's why I've been late getting back to the register sometimes. I just lose track of time in the bathroom.
Have you noticed any other changes in your mood or energy level recently that might be affecting how you feel about this spot?
Um... no, not really. I mean... I feel mostly the same. Just... tired sometimes, I guess, from working. But nothing else really.
Do you often feel that others are judging you or that you need to be perfect in order for people to accept you?
Um... no, not really. I don't think everyone is judging me or anything like that. And I don't need to be perfect. I just... I just don't like how it looks. That's all.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about that spot on your face?

Um... I don't know exactly. A lot, I guess. That's... kind of why I came in. I just keep getting stuck on this one uneven spot, like around my nose and cheek. Especially when I see photos or... or when I'm under those bright store lights at work. People say they don't see it, but... it just feels like it's the first thing the customers or my managers notice. So... yeah, I think about it a lot.

When you're thinking about that spot on your face, do you feel a strong need to do something — like checking your appearance, adjusting your hair, or comparing yourself to others — to feel better or less anxious?

Um... yeah, I guess I do things like that. Like, when I'm on my break at work, I... I usually go to the bathroom and just look in the mirror for a while. Just checking it. And I try to pull my hair forward a bit to cover that side of my face. Sometimes I... I look at the other girls who come through my checkout line and look at their skin. I don't mean to, but... sometimes I lose track of time doing all that, and I end up being a little late getting back to my register.
Do you think the uneven spot on your face is something that other people would notice, or do you think it's more something that only you can really see?
Um... I don't know. Like I said, people tell me they don't see it. But... I don't know, it just feels like they do. I can see it, so... I just assume they can too.
When you check the spot in the mirror or adjust your hair to cover it, does it feel like you *have* to do it to prevent something bad from happening, or because you feel intense anxiety if you don’t?

Um... I don't know about something bad happening. It's just... I just feel like I need to check it. If I don't, I just feel really uncomfortable, I guess. Like I can't stop thinking about it until I look.
Do you feel that this uneven spot on your face makes you look deformed or unattractive in a significant way?

Um... I don't know about deformed. But... yeah, unattractive, I guess. I just... I keep getting stuck on it. It's just this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek. I notice it a lot in photos, or... under those bright store lights at work. And... I don't know, even when people say they don't see it, it just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me. So... yeah.
Do you feel that your thoughts about this uneven spot on your face take up so much of your time or energy that it gets in the way of other things you need or want to do?

Um... I guess so. It's... it's been a little distracting at work. My manager actually said something the other day about me taking too long on my breaks. And... I guess I've been a bit slower ringing people up, too. I just... I'm really trying to get a promotion right now, and I'm worried this is just making me look... unreliable, I guess.
Do you think the uneven spot you’re concerned about is something that’s barely noticeable or something that most people would clearly see and comment on?

Um... well, like I said, other people tell me they don't see it. But... I don't know. To me, it just seems really obvious, especially under those bright lights at the store. I just feel like everyone else has to be seeing it too, even if they don't say anything.
